evidence: Draft judged: 'An Ethical Double Bind Question gives someone a choice between two safe things to do.' Read cold in CONTEXT (once, as the first sentence of the paragraph that follows 'Manipulative Double Bind Questions are set up so that whatever you answer, you end up doing what the speaker wants.'), it reads as the ethical counterpart of that definition, and it leads straight into the unchanged 'Ethical Double Bind Questions might be:' and the example, which does offer a choice of two safe options (warmth or space). So it follows from the sentence before it and fits what comes after. There is no pronoun in the draft: it names its subject in full, where his 'one' would have had to point back across the paragraph break at the plural 'Manipulative Double Bind Questions'; the capitals match 'Manipulative Double Bind Questions' above and 'Ethical Double Bind Questions' after. 'someone' (third person after the paragraph above's 'you') is the one small person shift and reads fine. Against SOURCE (his own words: 'An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes.', from 'A manipulative double bind traps every answer inside the speaker's agenda. An ethical one offers two genuinely safe routes.'): kept are the ethical kind, a choice of exactly two, and safe. Lost are 'genuinely' (his emphasis that the safety is real, set against the trap in the paragraph above) and 'routes' (now 'things to do', slightly narrower because the example's second option is a feeling, though allowing a feeling of space still reads as something to do). I judge that 'safe' alone still carries the contrast, because the paragraph directly above says what the trap is, and the draft adds no claim or fact ('someone' and 'a choice' are already implied by 'offers two routes'). The words replaced are his, so the card shows his first and he can keep them; the draft is plainer and longer than his compact sentence, a voice cost he can weigh, with 'genuinely' the one nuance of his that he may want back. It matches the_change (Emulate sample cn, no AI fix). Tells: I went through T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in its context and find none PRESENT. Considered and judged absent: T12 (there is a manipulative/ethical pair, but it is the pattern's necessary contrast and was in his published two sentences; the draft adds no matched pair of its own); T26 (the full term 'Ethical Double Bind Question(s)' now opens two consecutive sentences, the one stiff spot in the reading, but it is the article's defined term, the first needs its subject named and the second is the unchanged lead-in to the example, so each has a job); T02/T09 (definition, definition, example is the pattern-entry form of the unchanged text around it, and the draft adds no extra step to it); T06 ('safe things to do' is plain, not therapy-safe abstraction, and 'safe' is his word); T15 (a rewording of his sentence in plain words, no rare-synonym swap, and no AI skeleton for it to hide). Linter: the only finding, 'D9 follows the source order', is accepted: one sentence for one, the same point in the same place, and the example after it supplies the noticing, so there is nothing here for T13/T09 to catch. Note outside the verdict: the writer's ADMISSION.json says for T14/T15 that the sentence 'puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped'; nothing is put back here and 'genuinely' is dropped, so that evidence line is templated and wrong, though both rows are absent on my own reading.
